analysis: The PR is documentation-only. It adds a 'GDN prompt kernels by GPU' section to docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 527-554) and a paragraph to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 595-611). They describe a Gated DeltaNet four-row prompt kernel (GatedDeltaPrefill in libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../GatedDelta.swift) that is selected per process by a bit-exact probe against the stock gated_delta_step, with a fallback to the stock kernel. The docs also describe the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED override. No code, wire fields, authorization, attestation, key custody or encryption paths change. I checked the claims against the threat model for security impact. T-041/A-001: the docs say recurrent checkpoint bits are preserved, so prefix-cache checkpoint capture, HMAC-keyed lookup tags, salt scoping and the TTL are unchanged. The probe adds about 16 MiB of transient memory once per kernel instantiation and process. The docs say no load quotation, activation floor, KV grant or capacity field changes, so the coordinator memory-policy contract (T-007/TB-002 reporting) stays compatible. The env override is a local operator control inside the existing operator-controlled TB-003 boundary and grants no new authority. Unverified: the actual kernel implementation and probe code are not in the supplied evidence, so the bit-exactness and unchanged-memory claims rest on documentation and are not independently confirmed. The docs do not change any control, so this is not a regression. A follow-up review of the code PR that introduces GatedDelta.swift should check probe determinism, side-channel timing (the kernel choice could shift TTFT, which is only a minor change to the accepted SEC-035 oracle), and the fail-closed fallback.
